description: Committee recommends ending newspaper public notice advertising.
Removes public notice for intersection and median changes.
Clarifies notice required before first Council or Committee meeting.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
Taxpayers will save on significant annual public notice advertising costs.

description: Recommend $450,000 for 170 31st Street West shelter infrastructure.
Funds sidewalk, fence, and communication activities for 60-bed shelter.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
Staff explained city's "modest support" for province's "significant investment" in shelter.
Caswell Hill residents, local schools, and businesses are directly affected.
How the 250-meter shelter buffer zone was determined remains unanswered.
Local schools, businesses, and a convalescent home oppose the shelter location.
City administration promised not to fund shelter operations or social services.

speakers.name: Don Scott
speakers.summary: Don Scott, representing Western Academy, expressed concerns about the proposed permanent shelter site, highlighting ongoing issues with homelessness in the area and potential impacts on local schools, businesses, and community safety.
said: Homeless issues already impact nearby schools and businesses.
Proposed shelter will attract more homeless, exporting downtown problems.
Location will irrevocably change Caswell neighborhood; council should rethink it.

description: City explores central navigation hub to address homelessness.
Study proposes network of hubs for coordinated services.
Potential costs range from $9 million to $32 million.
Partnership with province is essential for implementation.

chips.text: Mayor Block emphasized a central hub is crucial for homeless individuals to access services.
How mini-hubs with civic facilities would alleviate service duplication remains unclear.
Over 80% of homeless individuals identify as Indigenous, needing cultural services.
Administration will provide a roadmap and status updates by Q2 2026.
